Katori was sunk by 16 inch gunfire from USS Iowa during a raid on Truk Show less Read more Like 4 Dislike Reply 1 reply Hide replies 1 reply Comments 98 Top Show featured comments Newest Show recent comments, including potential spam In this video Transcript Description USS Kearsarge – America’s Weirdest Battleship 1.9KLikes45,428Views2024Nov 12 The pre-dreadnought era was a time of great experimentation. No navy was quite sure what they were doing. And you can see this in some weird designs, as sail moved to steam. And iron to steel. Such as the French Floating Hotels (tm). In the United States, this experimenting resulted in USS Kearsarge. And, most importantly, her double-stack turrets. Something that would later reappear on the Virginia-class, as well. This was done to get the greatest amount of firepower, on the smallest hull possible. A compromise, to allow for the fitting of a heavy 5-inch battery on the side. It...was interesting, if not particularly effective. However, it also wasn't the only thing unique to this ship. After all, she would endure until the 1950s as a massive floating crane ship. Certainly one of the stranger stories out there.
